text: Distinguish partition-mutex contention from session-checkout serialization. OperationContextSession may wait because only one user can check out a session at a time; increasing partitions does not remove that exclusivity. SERVER-37499 describes a historical same-session exchange deadlock and explicitly says the scenario had not been observed. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

text: serverStatus excludes lockContentionMetrics by default. Request db.runCommand({serverStatus:1,lockContentionMetrics:1}) for aggregate tags or {serverStatus:1,lockContentionMetrics:{listAll:1}} for individual mutexes. total counts acquisitions, contentions counts acquisitions that waited, and waitCycles measures waiting in CPU cycles, not microseconds. text: logicalSessionRecordCache.sessionCatalogSize reports catalog population, including cached transaction or retryable-write state on mongod. It is not a direct measure of mutex contention or of simultaneously executing requests; correlate population with contention counters and operation latency. text: For blocked-thread investigation, off-CPU stack analysis complements CPU profiling, which misses time asleep waiting for locks. Off-CPU duration can also include scheduler delay after wakeup, and tracing overhead can alter the workload. This is general diagnostic methodology, not proof of a MongoDB session-catalog bottleneck.
